name: Refugio de la calle Serranos, Valencia
story: One of more than 50 public shelters built in Valencia against the raids, which Italian bombers based in Mallorca carried out from 1937 to 1939. Begun on 22 June 1937 at Calle Serranos 25, beside the medieval Torres de Serranos, it held about 400 people in three reinforced-concrete chambers under a roof more than 1.5 m thick. With the shelters at Calle Alta (Falla Ripalda–Sogueros), Bombas Gens and Massarrojos, it forms part of the city's network of visitable shelters. Their Art Deco 'REFUGIO' lettering has become an emblem of Valencia's wartime design.
see: Three concrete chambers with original features and interpretation panels.
plan: Free guided visits on Saturday and Sunday at 13:00 (none in August), by reservation on 962 081 390.
